title: Grateful Dead Live at Shrine Auditorium on 1968-08-23
lineage: 8 track multitrack Reels> Sonic Wizardry > DAT > Cassette > DATs > CDRs > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1968 show with stellar Alligator > Caution > Feedback suite and soaring Dark Star, captured on a multi‑track soundboard that’s mostly clear despite occasional mud.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the band’s peak ’68 outings – tight jams, blistering The Eleven, powerful Dark Star, and an unforgettable Alligator‑Caution‑Feedback sequence.  Listeners note the multi‑track SBD source provides excellent detail, though a few tracks sound muddy or have minor tracking glitches from two tape sources.  Overall the show’s energy and musicianship far outweigh any technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Average of >20 reviews is ~4.6; most praise the music and only minor recording complaints, giving a strong combined show‑plus‑recording score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multi‑track SBD with occasional mud and slight tracking inconsistencies (two tape sources, minor glitches), but overall clear and detailed; no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Despite a confusing filler from another date, the core 8/23‑68 set flows tightly with strong segues (Alligator into Caution, Cryptical into The Other One) and showcases the band’s peak improvisational stretch.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise Jerry's guitar tone, calling his lead on Dark Star “beautiful” and noting a tender solo during Alligator.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is repeatedly called “amazing”, “the bass copilot” and praised for powerful, melodic lines throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is highlighted as “great” and “bluesy”, providing a key part of the Alligator/Caution suite.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey receive high marks – “perfect”, “weave a tapestry in percussion”, and are described as driving the jams with force.
